what: The heuristic precomputes CVRP task structure once: customer/depot facts are discovered from semantic loc()/visited() fact names, load() and vehicles() numeric IDs are found once, customer demands/capacity/max_vehicles are read from initial numeric values, and travel costs are extracted primarily from grounded visit, visit-via-depot, and return-to-depot operators using metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. Fallback PNE travel-cost parsing is used only for missing arcs. It precomputes direct and via-depot cost matrices plus sorted nearest-neighbor lists. During evaluation it reads the current numeric state and visited facts, finds the current location, computes remaining demand, checks resource infeasibility, then runs a state-dependent capacitated greedy completion starting from the current location/load/vehicles. It adds a capacity/fleet pressure component and the estimated final return-to-depot cost.
why: The CVRP client instances are fleet-limited, depot-centered, capacitated, and have heterogeneous demands and dense explicit travel costs. A pure unvisited-count or depot-distance heuristic ignores whether the current vehicle can serve the next customer directly or must use visit-via-depot. This design therefore reconstructs costs from grounded operators, distinguishes direct visits from depot reloads, and re-anchors a nearest-neighbor completion from the actual current state every evaluation. The capacity and vehicle components are motivated by the small fleet and heterogeneous demand pattern; the precomputed matrices and sorted neighbor lists are appropriate because instances are tens of customers, making one-time O(n^2) construction cheap while keeping per-state evaluation fast.
instance_patterns: Fleet-limited capacitated routing with a single depot and multiple vehicles
Dense explicit travel-cost matrix between depot and customers
Heterogeneous customer demands that interact with vehicle capacity
Depot reloads appear as visit-via-depot actions distinct from direct visits
Tens of customers, allowing O(n^2) precomputation and cheap repeated greedy simulation
design: Operator-based travel cost reconstruction from grounded actions
Precomputed distance matrices and sorted nearest-neighbor lists
Capacitated greedy routing completion anchored at the current state
Explicit capacity and fleet-pressure heuristic components
complexity: O(n) for reading visited facts and numeric state plus at most O(n^2) in the worst-case greedy simulation over pre-sorted neighbor lists; no sorting or task rescanning occurs during compute_heuristic().
fallbacks: Travel costs are primarily extracted from grounded operators. If any direct or via-depot arcs remain missing, the constructor attempts fallback recovery from numeric variable names containing travel-cost() and travel-cost-via-depot(). Missing customer-to-customer arcs may then be filled from via-depot costs or depot legs when already known. Essential loc/visited/load/vehicles discovery failures cause construction to fail with a clear HeuristicBuildError.
known_limitations: The greedy completion is not globally optimal and may overestimate or underestimate in states where a different future route would be much cheaper.
If demand or capacity numeric variables are compiled into opaque PNE expressions, capacity pressure degrades because demands may default to zero and capacity may remain effectively unbounded.
The heuristic does not perform an exact feasibility proof beyond remaining demand versus total fleet capacity, so some dead-ends may be detected only during the greedy simulation.
